statement.text:
Let p be a prime number. A group Γ is called p-Jordan if there exist
constants J and e such that any finite subgroup G ⊂ Γ contains a normal abelian
subgroup of order coprime to p and of index at most J · |G(p) |e . (For example by the
results of Brauer–Feit and Larsen–Pink, for any field K of characteristic p the group
GLn (K) is p-Jordan with e = 3.) Let the p-Jordan exponent e(Γ) of the group Γ be
the infimum of all constants e for which the above bound holds for some constant
J = J(e).
    a) Is it true that this infimum is always attained?
    b) Is it true that e(Γ) ⩽ 3 for any p-Jordan group Γ?                  C. Shramov
